title: The Unexpected Group Chat
premise: Ulyana Blackwood has kept her head down at Ashgrove Academy for fifteen years—first as a scholarship kid, now as the school's IT aide—while her anonymous coding account quietly documents the board's buried secrets. When the academy's legendary ghost begins leaving notes addressed to her by name in ink that shouldn't exist, Ulyana discovers the 'ghost' is a group chat of five students and one dead girl's archived messages, all pointing to a cover-up the board sealed a decade ago. As the chat's members become her first real found family—and one of them, Theo, becomes something more—Ulyana must choose between the safety of invisibility and exposing the truth before graduation, even though the last person who tried died for it. In the end, she releases the archive at graduation itself, the board falls, and she finally signs her real name to her work.
about_author: Freya Reyes is a former school IT technician from the Pacific Northwest who writes young adult fiction about quiet kids who know too much. She credits a decade of late-night group chats with teaching her that found family can be typed as easily as spoken.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Watches the Logs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet her meticulous double life: daytime IT aide, nighttime anonymous archivist of Ashgrove's buried scandals. A routine server audit turns up a file she didn't create, dated the year a student named Marisol Vega drowned. Emotional beat: the chill of being watched by the past.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The first ghost note appears on her monitor's glass—her real name, in silver ink that smears like mercury and won't wipe off. She checks cameras: no one. Beat: fear curdling into fascination as the note says only, 'You found her file. Good.'

chapters.title: The Legend of Room 114
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, a charming troublemaker, recounts the Marisol Vega ghost story to his friends for the hundredth time—then goes quiet when he realizes the details he's inventing keep coming true. Beat: the fun of a legend turning into dread he can't share.

chapters.title: Five Names, One Chat
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A second note contains a QR code leading to an encrypted group chat: Theo, Priya, Deshawn, Wren, and a silent account labeled M.V. The chat knows things about each of them they've told no one. Beat: wary, electric connection—strangers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, a board member's daughter, admits she found a sealed settlement file linking Marisol's death to a hushed-up facilities scandal. The chat agrees to investigate. Beat: the first taste of shared purpose, and the terror of what her father might do if he finds out.

chapters.title: Rules of a Haunting
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The group sets rules: no names outside the chat, meet only in Room 114, trust no adults. Ulyana breaks her own fifteen-year rule by showing up in person. Beat: the aching novelty of being expected somewhere.

chapters.title: Deshawn Knows the Halls
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. The custodian's son maps every camera blind spot and locked door, revealing the east wing was renovated the summer after Marisol died. Beat: pride in being useful, undercut by guilt—he once saw a worker crying in that wing and said nothing.

chapters.title: M.V. Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The silent account finally posts: a scanned page of Marisol's real diary, describing a flooded sub-basement and a teacher who told her to stay quiet. Wren, a skeptic, runs the metadata—it's authentic and fifteen years old. Beat: the ghost becomes a person, and grief enters the chat.

chapters.title: Theo's Debt
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses his scholarship depends on staying invisible to the board—his father was the contractor whose shoddy drainage work caused the flood. Beat: love against duty as Theo realizes helping Ulyana could cost his family everything.

chapters.title: The First Warning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana's anonymous archive is wiped from the server; a board lawyer 'casually' interviews her. Someone inside knows. She suspects the chat has a leak—or a sixth member. Beat: paranoia cracking her new trust, the old loneliness rushing back.

chapters.title: Priya's Father
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts her father; he admits the settlement but claims it protected the school, not the guilty. He gives her an ultimatum: stop, or lose her college fund. Beat: the crushing arithmetic of duty, and her quiet decision to defy it.

chapters.title: Room 114 at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The five meet in person for the first time, and behind a loosened wall panel find Marisol's actual diary—physical, water-stained, real. The chat account M.V. goes permanently offline. Beat: the ghost's work is done; the living are on their own now.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Was Careful Of
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback chapter: why Ulyana spent fifteen years invisible—a childhood incident where her testimony destroyed a teacher and taught her that truth has a body count. Beat: the wound beneath her caution, finally shown.

chapters.title: Theo, Off the Record
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A rooftop scene: Theo and Ulyana, almost-kiss interrupted by his confession that his father's company is named in the diary. Beat: love against duty sharpening—she may have to expose the man whose signature pays for Theo's future.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. Deshawn discovers his keycard was cloned—the leak isn't a person but the building's own 'smart' renovation system, still logging to a board-owned account. Beat: relief that no friend betrayed them, horror that the school itself is the informant.

chapters.title: Wren's Proof
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren authenticates the diary against archived maintenance records: the flood was reported, the sub-basement sealed with students' belongings inside, and Marisol's death ruled accidental despite evidence of a blocked exit. Beat: cold, clarifying fury.

chapters.title: Graduation Is in Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The board moves to expel Priya and revoke Theo's scholarship preemptively. The chat must choose: scatter safely or publish before graduation, when alumni press and families will be watching. Beat: the point of no return, chosen together.

chapters.title: The Sub-Basement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The five break into the sealed sub-basement and find the flooded archive room—Marisol's belongings, and a maintenance log proving the exit was chained. Deshawn sprains his ankle; they barely escape as the board's security sweeps in. Beat: terror, solidarity, and proof in hand.

chapters.title: Everything Ulyana Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cornered in the server room, Ulyana faces the head of the board alone—and chooses to stop being careful, restoring her full fifteen-year archive and the diary scans to every screen in the school. Beat: the quiet girl finally, deliberately, makes noise.

chapters.title: Commencement
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At graduation, the truth cascades: the archive goes public, alumni journalists swarm, the board resigns mid-ceremony, and Priya reads Marisol's name aloud from the stage. Beat: catharsis—the dead girl finally witnessed by everyone.

chapters.title: Signed, Ulyana Blackwood
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Aftermath: Theo's family makes restitution, the scholarship is rebuilt, and Ulyana publishes her first bylined investigation—her real name attached for the first time. A last note in silver ink on her monitor: 'Thank you. You can rest now.' Beat: grief and peace entwined.

chapters.title: The Group Chat That Stayed
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, chat-log format. One year later: the five, scattered at colleges, still text daily. They've renamed the chat 'Room 114' and added a pinned message—Marisol's diary's final line. Beat: found family enduring past the mystery, love outlasting duty.
